Elena — thanks for the note and sorry for the disruption. Quick acknowledgement: we’re treating this as a production incident and we will deliver a consolidated timeline, root cause summary, and remediation commitments by EOD Monday (2028-04-22).

High-level so you have immediate context:
- Impact window we’re tracking: 08:48–09:17 PT.
- Visible customer impact: increased per-token latency and intermittent 504s for ~12% of requests to the model route you use (model: redwood-instruct-v1, route: /v1/generate).
- Preliminary cause: transient imbalance in autoscaling + delayed KV cache warm-up after a model swap. We are working on a definitive RCA.

We will include: the full timeline, server-side logs (sanitized), a remediation checklist we’ll implement platform-side, and recommended changes for Avery’s retry/backoff settings so you can harden client behavior.

Would you be available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow (Apr 21) to walk through the timeline before we finalize the write-up? If not, we’ll send the full packet by email.

Best,

Subject: Post-incident packet: timeline, RCA summary, and next steps (Avery)

Elena / Samir — thanks for taking the time earlier. Attached is the initial post-incident packet. Below is a concise executive summary and the action items we will execute: 

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- Incident window: 2028-04-20 15:48:00–16:17:32 UTC (08:48–09:17 PT).
- Symptom: sustained latency increase and intermittent 504s for the redwood-instruct-v1 route affecting ~12% of requests.
- Root cause (short): an autoscaler configuration edge case caused a transient under-provisioning of inference workers during a rolling model swap; concurrent delayed KV-cache population made early requests fall back to slower execution paths.
- Customer data exposure: none — no plaintext customer inputs were shared externally. Logs delivered are sanitized and limited to request IDs/samples per your request.

Timeline (abridged)
- 15:45 UTC: scheduled model swap rollout begins for a separate capacity rebalancing job.
- 15:48 UTC: monitoring alarms begin for per-token latency on the shared pool servicing your route.
- 15:50–16:05 UTC: autoscaler attempts to spin new workers but a race with the rollout controller resulted in 3 of 12 expected workers being delayed by ~30–75s.
- 16:05 UTC: transient 504s spike as requests hit under-provisioned workers with cold KV caches.
- 16:12 UTC: mitigation initiated — abort rolling swap and trigger immediate warm-start of standby pool.
- 16:17:32 UTC: latency and error rates return to baseline.

Technical root cause details
- Autoscaler bug: under certain VM termination sequences, the autoscaler logic under-counted in-flight replacements, so it did not trigger the immediate secondary scale-out. This is a control-plane race condition.
- Cache warm-up: when the new workers came online they required KV cache population for your typical prompt prefix distribution; cold cache meant higher per-token compute and higher tail latency.

Actions we will take (platform commitments) — timeline and ownership
1) Immediate (next 48 hours) — engineering
- Hotfix autoscaler counter logic and deploy to production (owner: infra team; ETA: 2028-04-23)
- Add defensive guard to prevent model swap and autoscale decisions from taking place on the same worker pool (owner: runtime team; ETA: 2028-04-24)

2) Short-term (2 weeks) — engineering + SRE
- Add a KV-cache warm-start path: pre-warm popular prefixes during worker boot (owner: runtime; ETA: 2028-05-05)
- Add improved monitoring: instrument expected worker counts vs. desired counts and alert on divergence (owner: observability; ETA: 2028-05-01)

3) Customer-facing recommendations (immediate)
- Backoff: add jittered exponential backoff for 5xxs with a max retry of 3 for streaming requests.
- Prefetch: if you have predictable prefixes, warm representative requests during low-traffic windows to reduce cold-start exposure.

Compensation and next steps
- We will apply a one-time service credit equivalent to 5% of April usage for the affected routes once the RCA is finalized (owner: finance/CS; action: Vivek will confirm).
- Attached: sanitized logs (server-logs-2028-04-20.zip) and the narrative RCA (avery_teardown_rca_v1.pdf).
- Proposed follow-up: 30-minute technical debrief with SREs and runtime engineers on Apr 24 at 10:00 PT (please confirm).

If you want additional artifacts (trace spans, full request samples), we can provide them under your NDA/secured link — let us know the level of detail you need.

Thanks again — we appreciate your patience and will keep you posted as fixes ship.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
